newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Dollar/Swiss rises to 1.48 francs at close.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/Swiss rises to 1.48 francs at close.

text.p: The dollar rose briefly to the key 1.48 Swiss franc level just as trade was closing here, setting new three-year highs.
On a weekly chart, it was the highest level for the dollar against the Swiss currency since it traded up to 1.48 francs in the week of February 20, 1994.
The franc fell steeply after the U.S. unit broke above 1.47 francs in the Far East overnight. A U.S. holiday kept business thin.
"It is very thin because the U.S. has President's Day holiday. I think there were stop loss orders at 1.4775, and at 1.4800 francs," said one Swiss-based dealer.

The dollar fell briefly overnight when a Japanese wire service reported the Japanese may act alone if they chose to intervene to support the yen against the dollar. The dollar later managed to shake off market nervousness and recover.

The mark was also firm, trading up to levels during the day against the Swiss franc which were the highest for the German currency since early December 1993. But Swiss traders said both dollar and mark may be starting to look toppish.
The mark ended near key resistance seen at 87.10 Swiss centimes.
*The dollar closed at 1.4794/4799 francs versus 1.4612/4622 at Friday's close and 1.4730/4740 at Monday's open.
*Mark closes at 87.10/13 Swiss centimes versus 86.68/69 at Friday's close and 86.93/95 at Monday's open.
